chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Malik ibn Ashyam, from Ismail ibn Bazi' who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'For me there is a young daughter whose regularity (of menstruation) is lifted.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Dye her head with the henna so the menstruation would be returning to her.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I did that, so the menstruation returned to her.'

key_terms.ارْتَفَعَتْ عِلَّتُهَا: Her ailment/condition was lifted; here referring to the cessation or irregularity of menstruation.
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: Menstruation, the monthly bleeding in women.
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءُ: Henna, a plant used for dyeing and traditional remedies.
key_terms.فَتَاةٌ: A young girl or maiden, typically referring to a pre-pubescent or early pubescent female.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended remedy for a young girl whose menstruation has stopped or become irregular according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) prescribes henna dyeing as a practical remedy for a young girl whose menstruation had ceased or become irregular, a condition often associated with delayed puberty in classical medical understanding. The narrator’s confirmation that her menstruation returned after following this advice highlights the integration of prophetic tradition with empirical observation in Shia jurisprudence and medicine. This narration is frequently cited in discussions regarding the physical signs of reaching the age of maturity (*bulugh*) and the use of natural substances for regulating bodily functions.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman Bin Rusheyd, from Malik Bin Asheym, from Ismail Bin Yazi’e who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘For me there is a young daughter whose regularity (of menstruation) is lifted’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Dye her head with the henna so the menstruation would be returning to her’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did that, so the menstruation returned to her’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rashid from Malik ibn ‘Ushaym from ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ who has said the following: “

I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘My young daughter does not experience Hayd (menses) anymore.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Apply hair dye to her head with henna; her Hayd (menses) will return.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘She followed the instruction and her Hayd (menses) came back.’”
